chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated via his chain from Abdillah ibn Sinan, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Muhammad ibn Isa from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Udhaynah and Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding the woman who gives birth: Is it permissible for her to marry before she becomes pure? He said: When she gives birth, she may marry, but it is not permissible for her husband to have intercourse with her until she becomes pure. It is also possible that the limit was established for her because she was still in the waiting period of her husband who died for her, because anyone in this situation needs to observe the longer of the two waiting periods. If she gives birth before the waiting period ends, she needs to complete four months and ten days. And if four months and ten days have passed for her, she waits for her childbirth after that. This indicates that.

key_terms.الْأَجَلَيْنِ: the two periods (referring to the choice between time-based and event-based iddah)

ai.seo_question: Can a woman who gives birth during her iddah remarry immediately, and when can her new husband consummate the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the fiqh of 'iddah for a widow who gives birth, establishing that the waiting period is determined by the longer of the two durations: childbirth or the standard four months and ten days. It distinguishes between the validity of the marriage contract, which can occur immediately post-partum, and the permissibility of consummation, which is deferred until the full 'iddah concludes. This ruling ensures the woman's lineage is clear and aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of combining waiting periods in cases of simultaneous causes.
